newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-NIGERIA GIVEN CUP REPRIEVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIA GIVEN CUP REPRIEVE.

text.p: Nigeria have had their ban on competing in the African Nations' Cup cut in half, effectively allowing them back into the qualifying competition for the finals in the year 2000.

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) said Nigeria's original four-year suspension, imposed in February after their failure to turn up for the finals in South Africa at the start of the year, had been reduced to two years.
The decision was made at a CAF executive committee meeting in Cairo at the weekend.

CAF also announced the creation of an African Champions' League from next year, disqualified Burundi from the youth championship and held over a decision on Burkina Faso's hosting of the next Nations' Cup finals in 1998.
The reduction of Nigeria's ban came after an appeal by both the Nigerian football association and their Congolese counterparts.

Nigeria, the defending champions, refused to take part in the Africa Nations' Cup in South Africa in January after a diplomatic spat between the two countries over Nigeria's execution of writer Kan Saro-Wiwa and nine others late last year.
They were slapped with the four-year ban by an indigant CAF and threatened with expulsion from the 1998 World Cup qualifiers in France but the African body later softened its stance.
Nigeria will now be able to enter the qualifiers for the 2000 finals in Zimbabwe after having been excluded from the draw for the 1998 qualifiers, which kick off next month.
CAF also announced the creation of an African Champions' League, modelled on the successful, and lucrative, counterpart in Europe.
The competition will start next year and see the eight quarter-finalists divided into two groups with the winners going through to a two-leg final.
The two earlier rounds of the competition will still be played on a two-leg knockout basis, said CAF, who hope to attractive sizeable sponsorship for the tournament.
"But the Champions' League will start in 1997 even without sponsors," they added in a press release issued on Monday.

Burundi, who were surprise qualifiers for the last world under-20 champonship in Qatar in 1995, have been disqualified from the 1997 qualifiers because of an air embrago placed on the tiny east African country after a recent coup d'etat.
Burundi were scheduled to travel to Tanzania this weekend for their first round, first leg match but teams have been unable to leave the country because of the travel ban.
Earlier this month, the Burundi national team were disqualified from the 1998 African Nations' Cup qualifiers because they could not go to the Central African Republic.

The CAF executive committee also studied a report on Burkina Faso's progress in organising the next Nations' Cup finals in 1998 but CAF gave no details save to announce that another delegation is to travel there "in the coming months".
